title: 5T OTA
description: The five-transistor OTA sized by half-circuit: an input pair device at half the tail current, a mirror-load device (pick its child table to the opposite polarity; set ld_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS table), and the tail source. Gain, bandwidth, slew, noise, offset, and the input common-mode range are all author math over the three children's operating points. The load child evaluates first so the input device's drain level (the mirror's diode $V_{GS}$ below the supply) is known; the tail reads the input device's $V_{GS}$ to find its own headroom.

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input CM at which the operating point is evaluated

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the mirror output device's vds

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current, noise, and the CM-low edge

params.name: gm_id_ld
params.note: mirror-load inversion: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset (both scale with the load's gm)

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: tail inversion: higher V* costs CM-low headroom

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs, used to place the tail node; retune until the input-bias-consistent guardrail is green

params.name: ld_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the load table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the mirror load at half the tail current. Its vgs (the diode drop) sets the input device's drain level; its gds at the output DC level loads the gain.

params.name: vds_l
params.note: output-side vds, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its drain sits one diode drop below the supply; its source sits one vgs below the input CM.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device carrying the full bias current; its saturation headroom sets the CM-low edge.

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node: one input vgs below the input CM

rows.name: Av
rows.note: half-circuit differential gain into the two output conductances

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: both pair devices and both mirror devices contribute, each at its own density: 2*(vn_pair^2 + vn_ld^2*(gm_ld/gm_in)^2) (simulation-verified two-sided total)

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, ld__W, L_ld, gm_id_ld)*ld__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the mirror pair's offset referred by the gm ratio

rows.name: cm_lo_edge
rows.note: lowest input CM that keeps the tail saturated

rows.name: cm_hi_edge
rows.note: highest input CM that keeps the input device saturated under the diode drop

rules.note: the spec'd CM-low must sit above the tail-saturation edge
the spec'd CM-high must sit below the input-saturation edge
the tail-node placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
